caption:
Employee engagement in India has fallen to a four-year low of 23%. Gallup's number, not mine.

The easy read is that people stopped caring. The accurate read is harder. Most of the disengaged professionals I work with care enormously. They prepare. They know the material better than anyone in the room. Then they say the thing, it lands flat, and eleven minutes later someone else says it louder and the room nods.

Do that for two years and you stop offering. That isn't apathy. That's a trained response to being unheard.

Engagement surveys measure the symptom. The mechanism is presence — how you hold the room before you speak, what your voice does under pressure, whether you can sit in silence long enough for your point to register.

Thirty-five years of command taught me this: authority is not granted by the table. It is carried to it. Bearing, tone, calculated silence. These are learnable. Start there.

topic.title: India's employee engagement falls to four-year low of 23%
topic.angle: Lumina's audience isn't disengaged from laziness but from being qualified and invisible — their ignored ideas are the lived mechanism behind Gallup's national number, which reframes a culture statistic as a solvable personal presence problem.
topic.why_now: Gallup's 'Rebuilding Indian Workplaces for the Future' report landed around mid-September 2026 and its quiet-quitting companion piece is even fresher, making it the single most-quoted India workplace data point still in active circulation.

rationale: A stark, text-only stat card lets the Gallup number carry the weight without decoration, matching the brand's plainspoken, no-nonsense authority.
